subject: LynxPay post-incident summary & verification request
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Zhou <amelia@lynxpay.com>, LynxPay Support <support@lynxpay.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: LynxPay post-incident summary & verification request

Hi Amelia / LynxPay team,

Thank you again for your patience while we completed the internal review of the November 20 service disruption that impacted a subset of LynxPay inference requests. Attached you'll find a concise customer-facing RCA (lynxpay_rca_summary.pdf) and a machine-readable timeline (lynxpay_detailed_timeline.csv). Below are the high-level findings and the actions we propose to close the loop.

Executive summary
- Incident window (UTC): 2026-11-20 20:47–21:21 UTC.
- Impact: increased token latency and intermittent dropped tokens for ~6% of requests routed to model variants with sequence length >2048; visible across both streaming and batch endpoints.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back the control-plane routing change at 20:55 UTC, restarted affected serving pools, and applied a compatibility hotfix at 21:05 UTC. Normal throughput resumed by 21:21 UTC.
- Root cause (short): a control-plane rollout introduced an optimization that mis-evaluated model-variant compatibility for mixed-length workloads, causing requests to be routed to nodes without the expected KV-cache state; this produced repeated fallback behavior and occasional token loss.

What we did (completed)
- Reverted the deployment that introduced the optimization and replaced it with a guarded roll-forward.
- Performed a full replay against a LynxPay-representative workload in a staging cluster; results attached (raw-inference-logs-20261120.log).
- Preserved and exported audit logs and request traces (link in attachments).

Planned corrective actions (owners & ETA)
- Preventative guardrail: add a model-compatibility preflight check to the control plane (owner: platform-serving team, ETA: 2027-01-12).
- Canary and canary-size automation: automatic traffic-sample validation against KV-cache invariants (owner: runtime, ETA: 2026-12-08).
- Post-deploy verification: scheduled replay test and acceptance criteria for mixed-length workloads (owner: reliability, ETA: 2026-12-01).
- Compensatory credit proposal: 1.5 days of service credit; Jordan will handle the account paperwork if this is acceptable.

Security and data integrity
- We found no evidence of data exfiltration or PII exposure. All request payloads remained within our customer isolation boundaries. The preserved request traces are included for your review.

Next steps we request from LynxPay
- Confirm availability for a 60-minute verification walk-through the week of Nov 23 (we propose Tue 11/24 at 10:00 PT).
- Confirm whether you accept the proposed 1.5 days credit or would like us to route this to your procurement contact.
- Let us know any additional artifacts you'd like in the verification session.

Attachments: lynxpay_rca_summary.pdf (customer-facing RCA), lynxpay_detailed_timeline.csv (event timeline), raw-inference-logs-20261120.log (sanitized logs)

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

--
This message and attachments are intended for the named recipients and contain operational details about a service incident. If you are not the intended recipient, please notify sender and delete the message.

From: Amelia Zhou <amelia@lynxpay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LynxPay post-incident summary & verification request

Thanks, Olga — and thanks to the Redwood team for the quick rollback and the write-up. A few quick questions before we accept the credit figure and set a call: 

- Can you confirm explicitly that no customer request bodies or responses left Redwood’s environment during the incident?
- Were any third-party integrations (feature flags, config store) involved in the rollout path?
- Can you share a short excerpt from the preserved traces that shows the token-drop behavior (if available)?

We're available for a call Tue 11/24 at 10:00 PT; please calendar. On the credit: 1.5 days looks reasonable but procurement may ask for an itemized calculation — can Jordan loop in purchasing?
Appreciate the transparency.

—Amelia
Amelia Zhou
Head of Platform Reliability, LynxPay
amelia@lynxpay.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LynxPay post-incident summary & verification request

Olga / Amelia — quick technical clarifications to help with the verification session. Quoting Olga below for context:
> - Root cause (short): a control-plane rollout introduced an optimization that mis-evaluated model-variant compatibility for mixed-length workloads, causing requests to be routed to nodes without the expected KV-cache state; this produced repeated fallback behavior and occasional token loss.
What happened (technical detail)
- The rollout introduced a change to the routing predicate that prioritized node GPU memory locality for lower-length sequences. Under mixed-length traffic (some >2048 tokens), the predicate evaluated incorrectly for a small subset of routing keys resulting in routing to a node that had not fully warmed the KV cache for that model variant.
- The first few tokens in affected streams triggered fallback behavior in the runtime; subsequent retries hit the same mis-routed node for a short window, which created the token-drop symptoms and elevated latency. We saw correlated traces where the same request id experienced repeated model initialization paths.
Data exposure
- We performed a request-by-request audit for the impacted window and confirmed that no request payloads were transmitted to external networks and no storage layer writes occurred outside standard request tracing. We will provide the sanitized trace excerpts in the call and as attachments.

Logs & artifacts
- The attached raw-inference-logs-20261120.log contains canonical traces and timing markers. The CSV timeline maps control-plane events to node restart timestamps.

Controls we are adding (short list)
- Preflight model-compatibility check in the control plane (will block mismatched routing predicates).
- Canary traffic validation for KV-cache invariants (automated test).
- Extend our trace retention for three additional weeks for high-severity events for customer verification.

Credit rationale
- The 1.5-day credit is a straightforward operational credit (time-weighted) for the partial-service degradation window and customer impact. Jordan will draft the formal credit note.

Happy to walk through the raw traces on Tue.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Zhou <amelia@lynxpay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LynxPay post-incident summary & verification request

Hi Amelia — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming availability.
A few short answers and confirmations before the call:
- Data exposure: confirmed — no request bodies or responses left Redwood’s environment during the incident. Our audit is attached for your review.
- Third-party integrations: no external feature flags or config-store calls were involved in the rollout path that caused this behavior. The change was internal to our control-plane routing logic.

We have scheduled a 60-minute verification session for Tue, 2026-11-24 at 10:00 PT. Calendar invite will follow from Jordan. For the call we will:
  1) Walk through the customer-facing RCA PDF.
  2) Stream two sanitized trace excerpts from the preserved logs (one example showing token-drop behavior, one showing normal flow).
  3) Outline the guardrails and timelines and capture any LynxPay validation steps.

Jordan will circulate a formal credit note and procurement paperwork immediately after the call. If procurement needs an itemized impact matrix, Jordan will include the calculation.

If that schedule works, please reply "Confirm" and we'll send the invite. Thanks again for working with us on this — we'll ensure the verification session gives you the artifacts you need.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
